title: South Laredo Processing Center Costs Rise by $45 Million as Opening Slips to Late 2027
excerpt: The cost of the 300,000-square-foot processing center under construction on Cuatro Vientos Boulevard in South Laredo has climbed from $285 million to about $330 million, and its opening has slipped to November 2027, according to KGNS.
content:
The price tag on the processing center under construction in South Laredo has climbed by about $45 million, and its opening has slipped to November 2027, according to KGNS.

The 300,000-square-foot building along Cuatro Vientos Boulevard has been under construction for two years. It is expected to hold 1,000 people and is designed to bring Border Patrol, ICE, immigration officials and judges under one roof, KGNS reported.

The estimated cost has risen from $285 million to about $330 million, the station reported.

U.S. Rep. Henry Cuellar, who shared the updated figures, called for greater oversight of federal contractors and stricter penalties for delayed projects.

"It's late, and it's overpriced," Cuellar said.

The center is now expected to open in November 2027, rather than early in the year.

Denni Arnold of the Texas Civil Rights Project questioned why the money went to what Arnold described as another "detention facility" instead of the community, and called for more transparency about how the center will be used, particularly on Laredo's south side, where Arnold said there are fewer job opportunities and less investment.

Source: KGNS, "South Laredo processing center costs rise by $45 million, opening delayed," by Elena Stoica, Nov. 13, 2026. kgns.tv
